title: Generalize temporal coherence and continue validator decomposition
question: Should TimeSync apply the rev0090 temporal-coherence helper beyond scope composition and split additional validator concern families out of the monolithic validator?
why_now: rev0092 materially reduced digest-canonicalization risk. rev0093 through rev0102 generalized temporal checks across replay transparency, discovery freshness, authorized-verifier replay, retained exports, transport envelopes, lifecycle-authority recovery, aggregate artifact timing, profile compatibility timing, and policy-equivalence signature/evidence timing. rev0103 closed a transport-integrity binding-strength/protection seam. rev0104 closed a local assessment-time/actionability seam. rev0105 closed a signed profile-reference binding seam. rev0106 extracts evidence-summary semantics and closes a met-obligation usability seam. rev0107 extracts discovery version/digest binding semantics and closes a current-use bypass where freshness could bless returned discovery objects without aligned digest binding and version approval. rev0108 extracts transport capability semantics and closes an advertised-capability overclaim path for unknown profiles, private request items, and profile references on profile-forbidden adapters. rev0109 extracts aggregate revision-lineage semantics, aligns immediate-predecessor correction digests with publication cadence, and closes lineage sequence/revision-chain binding contradictions. rev0110 extracts aggregate privacy-control semantics and closes digest-class mismatches for profile-compatibility threshold equivalence and noisy-count privacy policy binding. The remaining risk is maintainability and fixture-family scale rather than a single obvious timestamp surface. rev0111 extracts external transparency receipt semantics, rejects wrong artifact-class bindings for validated statement/checkpoint/receipt digest fields, and applies the same checks to discovery-returned external receipt references. The remaining risk is maintainability and fixture-family scale rather than a single obvious timestamp surface. rev0112 extracts profile drift semantics and closes current-use digest-equivalence bypasses for digest-distinct and digest-rollover compatibility decisions. The remaining risk is maintainability and fixture-family scale rather than a single obvious timestamp surface. rev0113 extracts scope-composition guard/matrix semantics into tools/scope_composition_semantics.py, rejects current composed surfaces with wrong artifact-class source_digest bindings, rejects temporal source_time_digest values that do not match the surface source_digest they qualify, normalizes affected scope-composition fixtures, and adds three derivation-checked negative fixtures. The remaining risk is maintainability and fixture-family scale rather than a single obvious timestamp surface. rev0114 extracts policy lifecycle-authority digest binding semantics into tools/policy_authority_digest_semantics.py, rejects compact authority status/rotation/successor/recovery digests that bind the wrong artifact class, and adds three derivation-checked negative fixtures. The remaining risk is maintainability and fixture-family scale rather than a single obvious timestamp surface. rev0115 closes mutation-survivor wrong-bind seams in replay core digests, aggregate correction-authority digests, and transparency trust-policy lifecycle/drift digests. The remaining risk is repeatable mutation testing, digest-binding expectation-table drift, schema duplication, and fixture-family scale. rev0116 adds a checked mutation-survivor audit tool, wires focused wrong-bind probes into validation, closes discovery wrapper/nested drift decision, policy revocation, renewal-hint, lifecycle-rollup, and scope-composition matrix temporal wrong-bind survivors, and leaves only intentional checkpoint polymorphism in the exploratory bind-substitution scan. The remaining risk is broader mutation coverage for lifecycle/current-use/freshness fields, digest expectation-table drift, schema duplication, and copied fixture-family scale. rev0117 extends mutation-survivor coverage into lifecycle/current-use seams, extracts aggregate lifecycle decision-table row semantics, rejects non-current profile lifecycle actionability, no-compromise replay effects, retained-record current-use promotion, and canonical decision-table row drift. The remaining risk is mostly intentional downgrade semantics and schema/source duplication rather than known current-use mutation survivors. rev0118 tightens satisfied evidence-summary minimum coverage and replay witness/monitor checked-status semantics, extends mutation probes to 18, and adds four derivation-checked negatives. The remaining risk is broader mutation coverage for satisfied/current claims and schema/source duplication. rev0119 extends current-claim mutation coverage: assessment.validity_horizon must remain current for satisfied minimum-summary coverage, unsatisfied conformance cannot preserve actionable or conditional current use, fallback_mapping cannot survive a non-fallback conformance upgrade, accepted policy status cannot carry conditional actionability, mutation probes increase to 22, and four derivation-checked negatives are added. The remaining risk is broader portability/current-use mutation pressure in detached challenge and replay chains plus schema/source duplication.
next_best_moves: Extend mutation-survivor probes to detached challenge/replay portability and other satisfied/current claims only where exploratory scans show real survivor risk.
Prototype schema-source deduplication that renders the current standalone schemas while eliminating repeated inline subtrees.
Continue converting copied discovery/replay negative fixture families to derivation-checked base-plus-patch fixtures.
Add a small digest/lifecycle/evidence expectation table only if future mutation scans show repeated expectation drift across helpers.
Keep the safe-integer JCS subset fail-closed unless a future digest-bound surface deliberately admits JSON floats.

closure_reason: FT-0090 produced substantial validator decomposition and mutation hardening, but continuing it had become an internal-assurance treadmill. It is closed to redirect work toward an end-to-end evaluator and a real timing-system adapter. Closure does not assert that every schema-duplication or fixture-volume issue is solved.
